A test suite must be named for its target type using the {TargetType}Tests convention.

What The Standard says

“Testing” — The Standard's foundation examples name each test suite after the service under test. The {TargetType}Tests convention makes ownership and coverage discoverable. read it here.
“Unit Tests” — Controller examples follow the same subject-specific naming pattern with StudentsControllerTests. The analyser applies that repeated convention to every suite. read it here.

Why it matters

The {TargetType}Tests convention creates a direct, searchable relationship between production code and its verification. It removes naming ambiguity and makes missing or misplaced coverage easier to identify.

Bad code example

// Violates STXTEST003: A test suite must be named for its target type using the {TargetType}Tests convention.
class StudentsTests { } // Tests StudentService

Good code example

// Follows STXTEST003
class StudentServiceTests { }
